pages.x: In the Greek legend, Paris, a prince of Troy, carried off Helen, wife of King Menelaus of Sparta and the most beautiful woman in the world. Menelaus's brother Agamemnon, king of Mycenae, gathered a thousand ships and the greatest heroes of Greece to bring her back.

The Greeks camped on the beach and besieged Troy for ten years. Homer's Iliad tells only a few weeks of it: the quarrel between Agamemnon and Achilles, the best of the Greek fighters, and how Achilles, mad with grief for his friend Patroclus, killed Hector, Troy's champion, and dragged his body behind his chariot.

At last Odysseus thought of a trick. The Greeks built a huge wooden horse, hid soldiers inside and sailed out of sight. The Trojans dragged the horse into their city as a prize. That night the soldiers climbed out and opened the gates, and Troy burned. The Roman poet Virgil made a Trojan say: beware of Greeks bearing gifts.

The Odyssey follows Odysseus, who took ten more years to reach his home on Ithaca, past the Cyclops, the Sirens and the witch Circe, while his wife Penelope kept her suitors waiting. Aeneas, a Trojan who escaped, was said to have reached Italy, and the Romans claimed him as their ancestor.

The two poems are said to be the work of Homer, a blind poet of the 700s BC, though no one knows if he existed. They were sung for generations before they were written down, and every educated Greek and Roman learned them by heart.

In 1871 Heinrich Schliemann, a rich German businessman, dug into the mound of Hisarlik in Turkey, sure it was Troy. He found nine cities, one on top of another, and gold he called Priam's treasure, though it was a thousand years too old. Layers from around 1200 BC show a city that was burned.

Real or not, the Trojan War is the first great story of Europe. The Iliad and the Odyssey shaped Greek and Roman life and are still read, and we still speak of an odyssey, an Achilles heel and a Trojan horse, now also a kind of computer virus.
pts: Told in Homer's Iliad and Odyssey
A real burned city lies under the legend
Gave us the Trojan horse and the Achilles heel
